stem: A nurse provides home-safety teaching to a client who uses supplemental oxygen from an oxygen concentrator. Which client statement shows correct understanding?

options.A: I will keep the oxygen equipment away from open flames and heating sources, and no one will smoke near it
options.B: I can use the oxygen next to a gas stove as long as I turn the flow rate down
options.C: Petroleum-based products are safest to use around my nose while I am on oxygen
options.D: I can change my prescribed oxygen flow whenever I feel short of breath without contacting my provider

rationale: MedlinePlus home-oxygen guidance instructs clients to keep oxygen away from open fire and other heating sources and not to smoke while oxygen is in use. It also advises clients not to change or stop the prescribed oxygen flow without discussing it with the provider and to use water-based rather than oil-based products for dryness. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Teach core home oxygen safety: keep oxygen away from flames and heat, prohibit smoking near oxygen, and follow the prescribed oxygen plan rather than changing flow independently.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus
source_version_date: Current MedlinePlus patient instruction reviewed/updated 2026; accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Sections 'Using Oxygen' and home oxygen safety instructions: keep oxygen far away from open fire or other heating sources; do not smoke when using oxygen; do not stop or change oxygen flow without talking with the provider; use water-based rather than oil-based products for dryness
source_claim_supported: Home oxygen users should avoid open flames, heat sources and smoking, and should not independently change prescribed oxygen flow.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Home Safety, printed p.25 / PDF p.29: educate client on safety concerns; evaluate client care environment for fire and environmental hazards
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — home oxygen/fire safety
correction_summary: Removed the generic ventilation claim from the source item because concentrator placement and vent-clearance details are device-specific. Reframed the item around directly supported home-oxygen fire-safety teaching and replaced obvious distractors with realistic unsafe client statements.
audit_findings: A directly matches current federal patient-safety guidance. B retains an ignition hazard, C conflicts with guidance favoring water-based over oil-based products, and D conflicts with instructions not to change oxygen flow independently. The item avoids a universal distance, ventilation clearance, or equipment-placement number not directly required by the source. NCSBN 2026 explicitly supports home fire/environmental safety teaching. Independent second pass found one best answer and no unresolved conflict.
